title: Humane solution for Apolinarka cats — 8.2k signatures against institutional eviction
summary: Petition for a sustainable, humane solution for the cat colony at Prague's Apolinar hospital grounds has 8,183 signatures. Citizens demand institutions handle animal colonies humanely instead of eviction.
notes: 8,183 signatures as of 2026-08-14; top-3 trending on petice.com Aug 2026. Animal-welfare institutional-conduct asks recur (see tyrani-zvirat cluster).

title: Accessible services for people with autism — 20.3k signatures
summary: Petition for more accessible services for children and adults with autism has 20,279 signatures (e-petice.cz most-signed index). Families document missing care capacity — diagnosis waits, respite and social services.
notes: 20,279 signatures as of 2026-08-14 (e-petice.cz ?filt1=3 index). Fits recurring care-capacity cluster (child psychiatry, pediatricians) — care-access petitions keep reappearing.

title: Brno Dame na vas 2024 — 20.5k voters, 7 winners all ~4k+ votes, 2 of 7 are tree projects
summary: 8th Brno participatory budget: 20,493 voters (near the 20,676 record) split 35M CZK among 7 winning projects, each just above 4,000 votes. Two of seven winners are street-tree planting projects; rest: playgrounds/sport access, community garden, culture.
notes: 20,493 voters 2024; 74 finalist projects; winners incl. 'Stromy na Milady Horakove' and 'Stromy za stromy' (greenery x2), football-pitch access path, 'Fandr pro vsechny - ozivme hriste'. All-time PARO platform: 1,565 projects, 697,971 votes, 3.245bn CZK proposed value (paro.damenavas.cz; register already tracks civic-brno-paro).

title: dTest class-action campaign — 10k supporters in 4 weeks; 1 in 3 Czechs affected
summary: dTest's 'Za hromadne zaloby' campaign for a class-action law collected 10,000+ supporters within four weeks of launch; dTest survey: every third Czech faced a situation a class action would solve. Law finally effective July 2024, but dTest documents it remains unusable (financing model missing).
notes: 10,000+ campaign supporters in first 4 weeks (dtest.cz); survey claim 'kazdy treti Cech'. Post-2024 follow-up (e15, dtest clanek-11055): zero effective use — demand persists. Only major consumer-org petition machine in CZ (dTest 'proti smejdum' 2013: 13k).

title: eDoklady app — 2.6 stars from 1,800 App Store ratings; offline & acceptance complaints
summary: The state digital-ID app eDoklady (DIA) holds 2.6/5 from ~1,800 ratings on the Czech App Store two years after launch. Recurring review themes: no offline mode (works only via airplane-mode trick), app re-downloading expired old ID, few places accepting it, UI broken on small screens, no family/multi-ID support.
notes: 2.6 stars, 1,800 ratings (2026-08-14, v1.28.0). Complaint themes are feature demands: offline verification, doc-cache refresh, wider verifier coverage, multi-holder support. Google Play listing not statically fetchable (negative).

title: Mandatory CCTV in all slaughterhouses — 36.2k signatures
summary: Petition for mandatory camera systems in all Czech slaughterhouses shows 36,196 signatures on e-petice.cz (top of the most-signed index). Demand for enforcement/monitoring infrastructure, not politics.
notes: 36,196 signatures via e-petice.cz most-signed listing (?filt1=3), as of 2026-08-14. Related: anti-puppy-mill 17,347 on same index. Animal-welfare enforcement asks recur yearly.

title: Save Kukleny roundabouts in Hradec Kralove — 7.0k signatures on road redesign
summary: Petition to save the Kukleny roundabouts in Hradec Kralove from a planned arterial rebuild has 6,990 signatures. Residents contest state road design that removes locally valued safe intersections.
notes: 6,990 signatures as of 2026-08-14. Typical of recurring 'citizens vs. state road design' conflicts (cf. I/27 route opposition 309 on e-petice.cz).

title: Keep Line airport + air rescue base — 8.2k signatures in 3 weeks
summary: Petition against demolishing Plzen-Line airport for a VW gigafactory and for keeping the military air rescue (LZS) base collected 8,200+ signatures in ~3 weeks (2023) and was handed to the regional governor. Core fear: emergency-care coverage for W. Bohemia.
notes: 8,200 signatures at handover (~Jun 2023, date approx; CTK/stavebniserver). Separate e-petice.cz petition for keeping the Line LZS base: 1,408 signatures. Airport ultimately preserved after project fell through.

title: Menstrual leave in labor law — 33.5k signatures in two months
summary: Petition to introduce menstrual leave into Czech labor law collected 33,570 signatures within ~2 months of its June 2026 launch, addressed to government and MPSV. One of the fastest-growing CZ petitions of 2026.
notes: 33,570 signatures as of 2026-08-14; launched Jun 2026 (denikalarm.cz, refresher: 26k within weeks). Spain 2023 precedent cited. Employer-side pushback documented (podnikatel.cz, zdravotnickydenik.cz 2026-07).

title: Munipolis civic-communication platform — 1M+ users, 5,000+ municipal clients
summary: Munipolis (ex-Mobilni rozhlas) claims 1,000,000+ citizen users and 5,000+ municipal/organization clients across 5 countries after 15 years — the de facto standard channel for citizen reports and alerts in CZ towns. Absorbed the ZmapujTo reporting app.
notes: 1,000,000+ users; 5,000+ clients (site claims, 2026-08-14). Publishes NO public per-category report statistics (negative finding); only anecdata like Zlin 700+ resolved reports. Demand inference: thousands of municipalities pay for structured citizen-report intake.

title: Affordable rental housing program oversubscribed — applications froze the scheme in 9 months
money_note: Applications 20.1bn CZK vs. planned allocation; program suspended 2025-06-30 pending budget increase.
summary: The state Affordable Rental Housing program (launch Oct 2024) reported 5.1bn CZK of applications for 1,500 flats early on; by 30 Jun 2025 applications reached 326 projects for 20.1bn CZK, exceeding allocation, and intake was suspended pending more budget. Municipal/investor demand for rental-housing finance far outstrips supply.
notes: 5.1bn CZK / 1,500 flats (MF press release); 326 applications / 20.1bn CZK by 2025-06-30, program paused (SFPI/MF 2025 data). Institutional-level demand record complementing citizen-level Za bydleni signal.

title: Keep onco-urology surgery in regional hospitals — 851 signatures against decentralization rules
summary: Petition against 'de-centralization' limits that would move onco-urological operations out of regional hospitals has 851 signatures. Part of the recurring regional-hospital-service-cuts genre.
notes: 851 signatures as of 2026-08-14. Same-genre concurrent petitions: Bilovec hospital independence 248 (petice.com), Kadan hospital 23 (e-petice.cz). Hospital-cut petitions recur in every region; healthcare-access anxiety is structural.

title: Ostrava-Jih Nas Jih 2025 — 5.5k voters pick 9 projects; leisure & shade dominate
summary: 10th Ostrava-Jih participatory budget: 5,500 residents voted, 9 public-space winners + 1 courtyard (new 'Nas Jih za domem' line up to 10M CZK). Winning themes: all-age obstacle course, forest relaxation zone, badminton, family leisure park, sandbox shading.
notes: 5,500 voters (2025); 9 years cumulative: >30M CZK, 60+ realized projects; 2022 edition for comparison: 5,738 voters, 36 proposals. Ostrava MOaP district 2025: 7 proposals, 5 to public vote (participace.mobilnirozhlas.cz/nasobvod).

title: Recurring PB ask #2: play & casual-sport micro-infrastructure — top votes in 4 cities
summary: Playground/casual-sport micro-infrastructure is the single most voted PB category across cities: Plzen 1 winner ball-play track (372 votes 2026), Ostrava-Jih winner all-age obstacle course + badminton (2025), Brno funded pitch access + 'ozivme hriste' (2024), Praha 21 funded a 500k CZK rope playground (2025).
notes: 4 cities, same theme, 2024-2026: Plzen 372-vote winner; Ostrava-Jih top winner; Brno 2 of 7 winners; Praha 21 biggest single grant. Also school PB variants (Pebecko, decision21.cz) push identical asks. Structural: municipalities underprovide low-cost play/sport infra.

title: Recurring PB ask #1: street trees, greenery and shade — winners in Brno, Plzen, Ostrava
summary: Tree-planting/greenery/shade proposals win participatory budgets in 3+ cities: Brno 2024 had two tree projects among 7 winners (~4k votes each), Plzen 1 2026 tree+perennial planting took 215 votes (3rd), Ostrava-Jih 2025 funded a forest relax zone and sandbox shading. Citizens systematically buy urban greenery with their PB votes.
notes: Evidence: Brno 'Stromy na Milady Horakove' + 'Stromy za stromy' (2024, each >4,000 votes); Plzen 1 'Vysadba stromu a trvalek' 215 votes (2026); Ostrava-Jih 'Relaxacni zona v Belskem lese' + 'Zastineni piskoviste' winners (2025). 3 cities, 3 consecutive years = structural unmet need for urban greening.

title: Plzen 1 Rozhodnete sami 2026 — 1.1k voters, winner: ball-play track (372 votes)
summary: Plzen 1 participatory budget round 2 (voting 5 Jan-5 Feb 2026): 1,142 residents cast 1,976 votes over 9 projects for 1.5M CZK. Top asks: ball-play track (372), barefoot sensory path (265), tree & perennial planting (215).
notes: 1,142 voters, 1,976 votes, 9 projects. Full ranking incl. negative voting: dog meadow netted -159 (net-negative demand exists). Plzen 3 runs parallel scheme with 9M CZK over 9 quarters (rozhodnetesami.cz/plzen3).

title: Portal obcana app — 2.7 stars from 480 ratings; downloads, login and biometrics fail
summary: The official Portal obcana mobile app rates 2.7/5 from 480 App Store ratings. Recurring complaints: files 'download' with no way to open them, connection/login failures, broken Face ID/fingerprint — i.e., citizens want working mobile access to state services and don't get it.
notes: 2.7 stars, 480 ratings (2026-08-14, v1.23.0 of 11 Jun). Launched Apr 2024 (irozhlas). 'Moje dane' has NO standalone mobile app — tax filing routed through this app/web; mojedane portal maintains a dedicated outage 'sorry-page' (podpora.mojedane.gov.cz) — negative finding.

title: Czech Post branch closures — 105k signatures against cutting 300 branches
summary: Petition against closing ~300 Czech Post branches (3,220 -> ~2,100 network plan) gathered ~105,000 signatures from 840+ municipalities within weeks in spring 2023. Citizens demand physical service-point access, esp. for seniors and small towns.
notes: 105,000 signatures, 840-850 municipalities (Apr-May 2023; date approx = milestone report). Parallel local petitions: Havlickuv Brod, Praha Jizni Mesto (petice.com/nebertenampostu), Olomouc. Recurring theme: physical access to state/utility service points.

title: Prague 8-year gymnazium crunch — 5,000+ applicants for 1,737 places
summary: Over 5,000 Prague children applied for 1,737 eight-year gymnazium places in 2026 (capacity even fell 86 places y/y) — a ~3:1 documented demand overhang repeating every admissions cycle. Survey (Jun 2026): 14% of Prague parents had to pick a more distant school for capacity reasons.
notes: 1,737 places vs 5,000+ applicants (2026; other reporting cites 1,816 places); -86 places y/y; 14% forced to distant school (pedagogicke.info survey 2026-06). City negotiating with state over Stredocesky commuter load. Annual recurrence since ~2022.

title: Prague district participatory budgets — P1 4.5M+0.5M CZK, P15 445 voters, 7th editions
summary: Prague has no city-wide participatory budget; districts run their own: Praha 1 allocates 4.5M CZK civic + 0.5M school PB (2026, project presentations 25 Mar), Praha 15 ran its 7th edition with 445 voters in June. Structural: same instrument re-implemented district by district.
notes: P1: 4.5M + 0.5M CZK (2026); P15: 445 voters, 7th edition, pilot 2019 was 200k CZK/50k per project; P21: 2M CZK 7th ed. No city-wide scheme = fragmented civic-demand data (negative finding for aggregation).

title: Praha 21 Menime Ujezd 2025 — 10 proposals, 4 winners (rope playground, pier, skatepark lights)
summary: 7th Praha 21 participatory budget (2M CZK): 10 citizen proposals, 6 to vote, 4 funded — rope playground 'Monkey Town' (500k CZK), pond pier (160k), skatepark lighting (150k), park strip at Level (250.8k). Themes mirror other cities: play, water access, lighting.
notes: 2025 cycle (page undated; scanned 2026-08-14). 10 proposals -> 6 voted -> 4 winners, 150k-850k CZK each. 7th consecutive year = sustained district-level demand channel.

title: GP/pediatrician deserts — 24k adults + 6k children without a doctor in one region
summary: In Kralovehradecky kraj alone, 24,000 adults and 6,000 children have no practical doctor; ~340 pediatric practices closed nationwide in four years as retirements outpace replacements (>50% of pediatricians are 60+). Mayors openly recruit doctors with flats and subsidies — 'get us a doctor' is a municipal-election issue.
notes: 24,000 + 6,000 without GP (KHK); ~340 pediatric practices closed in 4 yrs; pediatricians 65+: 31.9% (2021) -> 34.6% (2023). Cheb/Sokolov patients travel 80 km (irozhlas 2024-05-29). Regions run subsidy programs (MSK 3M CZK, Ustecky 2025-26) = institutionalized demand.

title: Preserve diversity of preschool care — 16.6k + forest kindergartens 15.2k signatures
summary: Two petitions defending non-mainstream preschool care sit in the e-petice.cz all-time top 10: 'Save the diversity of preschool care' (16,637) and 'Save forest kindergartens' (15,168). Parents demand plurality of childcare forms against regulatory tightening.
notes: 16,637 + 15,168 signatures (e-petice.cz most-signed index, as of 2026-08-14). Same ask twice on one platform = recurring; pairs with chronic mainstream skolka capacity shortages.

title: Raise parental allowance — 15.3k signatures
summary: Petition to raise the parental allowance (rodicovsky prispevek) has 15,308 signatures on e-petice.cz. Recurrent inflation-cycle ask by parents on maternity/parental leave.
notes: 15,308 signatures as of 2026-08-14. Benefit-indexation petitions recur with each inflation wave; parental allowance was last raised 2024 after similar public pressure.

title: Save translation studies at Charles University — 8.3k signatures
summary: Petition against closing the translatology programme at Charles University's Faculty of Arts gathered 8,285 signatures within weeks. Recurring pattern: budget-driven programme cuts triggering alumni/professional mobilization.
notes: 8,285 signatures as of 2026-08-14; trending #2 on petice.com. Parallel same-faculty petition: theatre studies dept. autonomy 805. University programme-cut petitions recur yearly.

title: Higher penalties for animal abuse — 153.8k signatures, largest active petice.com petition
summary: Petition demanding higher criminal penalties for animal abuse has 153,806 signatures — the largest on petice.com. Part of a persistent animal-welfare enforcement cluster that keeps producing 15k+ petitions.
notes: 153,806 signatures (as of scan 2026-08-14). Cluster evidence: CCTV in all slaughterhouses 36,196 (e-petice.cz), anti-puppy-mill 17,347, case-specific 'Dixie' 34,796, Litomerice case 3,763. Recurrence across years and platforms = structural enforcement-gap perception.

title: Regional train service cuts — petitions recur across regions (2.9k, 5k, 3.5k signatures)
summary: Petition against cutting passenger trains on 12 Central Bohemian routes (2,862 signatures) demands preserved timetables, unified PID train/bus pricing and modular rolling stock. Same ask recurs region after region whenever timetables shrink.
notes: 2,862 signatures (count as of 2026-08-14; started 2021-07-02); line 210 had 390-658 daily passengers. Cluster: Kolin-area 5,000 signatures (2021, kolinsky.denik.cz), Ceske stredohori 3,500 (Radiozurnal), line 262 Skalice-Velke Opatovice 2,166 (e-petice.cz). Cross-region recurrence = structural rail-service anxiety.

title: Protect Vrbenske ponds from development — 1.4k signatures
summary: Petition to protect the Vrbenske ponds nature site near Ceske Budejovice from large-scale development has 1,366 signatures. One instance of the most recurrent CZ petition genre: greenfield/nature vs. developer.
notes: 1,366 signatures as of 2026-08-14. Genre recurrence on e-petice.cz same week: FVE Ralsko 565, wind Sazomin 73, wind Bystra 241, logistics center FCC Slustice 463, historic homes Ceske Budejovice 238.

title: Housing Support Act — 1.9k professional signatories, 161k homeless incl. 62k children
summary: The 'Za bydleni' appeal for passing the Housing Support Act (zakon o podpore bydleni) gathered 1,914 signatories incl. Chamber of Architects head, academics and social workers; the law passed its third reading 2025-04-16. Context cited: 161,000 people homeless (62,000 children), 1.3M in housing cost stress.
notes: 1,914 signatories; law timeline: gov 2024-06-12, 1st reading 2024-07-10, 2nd 2025-03-05, 3rd 2025-04-16. Housing-affordability asks recur across petitions, PB proposals and municipal programs.

title: PET bottle deposit-return scheme — 35.6k petition + 250k campaign supporters
summary: Zalohujme petition for a deposit-return system on PET bottles and cans was handed to Parliament with 35,596 signatures (Feb 2022); combined Zalohujme+Greenpeace campaigns counted ~250,000 supporters. Demand preceded the 2024-25 government bill.
notes: 35,596 signatures delivered 2022-02-14; 250,000 campaign supporters claimed. Government approved deposit scheme (4 CZK, ~11,000 collection points) in 2024 — demand validated by later legislation.

title: ZmapujTo: tens of thousands of illegal-dump reports since 2012, app folded into Munipolis
summary: ZmapujTo, the illegal-dump reporting app, states it mapped 'tens of thousands' of illegal waste sites since 2012 before being absorbed into Munipolis. Sustained citizen reporting volume documents a chronic municipal waste-enforcement gap.
notes: 'Desitky tisic' (tens of thousands) mapped dump sites 2012-2026 — order-of-magnitude only, no exact counter published (negative finding on data quality). Standalone app discontinued; reports now via Munipolis.

title: CNB consumer submissions 2025 — ~2,700 filings; non-bank credit complaints up sharply, 42 flag unlicensed lending
summary: CNB's 2025 supervision report counts about 2,700 public submissions: 1,107 against credit institutions (up 7% YoY, driven by payment accounts, AML friction and fraud), 1,100 in insurance (claims settlement leading, 2024 flood claims still unresolved), and 342 against non-bank consumer lenders - a sharp year-on-year rise including 42 reports of unlicensed lending. Complaints about revolving products with opaque terms are growing.
notes: Zprava o vykonu dohledu 2025 (dnft_2025_cz.pdf): 1 107 podani (uverove instituce, +7 %); 1 100 pojistovnictvi; 342 NPSU ('vyrazny mezirocni narust'), z toho 42 neopravnene poskytovani uveru; 61 platebni sluzby; 46 penzijni; 13 crowdfunding; AML/CFT narust; povodne 2024 nedokoncene likvidace.

title: Alcohol and tobacco sold to minors — violations in 43% of 1,902 inspections; decoy tests fail in almost half
summary: The Czech Trade Inspection reported (14 Aug 2026) that in Q2 2026 checks of the ban on selling alcohol and tobacco to minors it found violations in 819 of 1,902 inspections (43.1%), and in nearly half of the inspections using under-age decoys alcohol was actually sold or served to a person under 18. Age-verification practice in shops and hospitality is systemically failing.
notes: COI TZ 14.8.2026: 1 902 kontrol, poruseni v 819 (43,06 %); 'temer v polovine kontrol s mladistvymi figuranty byl prodan nebo podan alkohol osobe mladsi osmnacti let'.

title: Counterfeit goods — 14,354 items seized in Q2 2026 worth ~54M CZK, a 10x jump on Q1
money_note: Seized counterfeits valued at ~54M CZK (original prices) in Q2 2026; Q1 2026: 2,404 items / ~5M CZK
summary: The Czech Trade Inspection seized 14,354 counterfeit items with an original-price value of almost 54M CZK in Q2 2026, up from 2,404 items (~5M CZK) in Q1 - a tenfold jump quarter-on-quarter that documents persistent counterfeit distribution through marketplaces and stalls.
notes: COI TZ 30.7.2026: 14 354 ks padelku za temer 54 mil. Kc (Q2 2026); TZ 20.7.2026: Q1 2026 = 2 404 ks za temer 5 mil. Kc.

title: 28th regime — company-law fragmentation forces startups through 27 national systems
summary: Proposal for a single harmonised EU-wide legal regime for innovative companies, answering complaints that incorporating and scaling across 27 systems is slow and costly. Proposal feedback closed 25 Jun 2026; the initiative drew 2,518 feedback items including 1,470 OPC responses.
notes: 2,518 total feedback (OPC 1,470 + CFE 879 + proposal 169) — heaviest startup-policy response of the cycle; VCs, startup associations; CZ exposure: CZ startups incorporating in Delaware/Estonia today; legislative negotiation ongoing

title: AI strategy for cultural and creative sectors — AI disrupts creative work and rights
summary: Culture Compass deliverable laying out a strategic vision for AI use in cultural and creative industries, balancing innovation with creators' interests. Call for evidence open until 11 Sep 2026; 29 responses.
notes: 29 feedback; creative industries, rightsholders, AI firms; CZ exposure: CZ game dev and audiovisual sector, authors' rights vs genAI

title: Single banking market competitiveness — structural barriers limit cross-border banking
summary: Savings and Investments Union workstream assessing how EU banking supports economic competitiveness and which structural barriers block cross-border activity and market integration. Communication feedback open until 17 Sep 2026; 56 feedback items.
notes: 56 feedback; banks, fintechs; CZ exposure: CZ banking is foreign-owned (Erste/KBC/SocGen) — cross-border capital/liquidity rules directly affect CZ subsidiaries

title: Battery recycled-content methodology — rules for 2031/2036 targets must be workable
summary: Delegated act sets the calculation and verification methodology for mandatory recycled content (Li, Co, Ni, Pb) in batteries placed on the EU market. Feedback until 9 Sep 2026.
notes: 1 feedback so far; battery makers, recyclers, auto OEMs; CZ exposure: CZ auto supply chain and planned gigafactory projects face the targets

title: BEREC call on mobile network APIs — developer access to operator network capabilities
summary: BEREC gathers input on interfaces (network APIs) exposing mobile-network capabilities to developers and third-party services, a building block for the Digital Networks Act debate. Closes 26 Aug 2026.
notes: Open call for inputs, deadline 26 Aug 2026; telcos, CAMARA/GSMA ecosystem, developers; CZ exposure: CZ operators' API monetisation, app developers

title: BEREC roaming review input — does roam-like-at-home still work for consumers and MVNOs
summary: BEREC collects evidence for its 2027 opinion on the Roaming Regulation review, probing wholesale caps, fair-use and sustainability of roam-like-at-home. Closes 21 Aug 2026.
notes: Open call for inputs, deadline 21 Aug 2026; operators, MVNOs, consumer bodies; CZ exposure: CZ travellers/consumers and CZ MVNO wholesale economics

title: European Business Wallet — repeated paper/identity filings burden companies EU-wide
summary: Proposal for digital services letting companies interact with administrations once, digitally, across the EU (business wallet), cutting administrative costs. Proposal feedback closed 6 May 2026; 156 feedback items across stages.
notes: 156 total feedback (95 CFE + 61 proposal); chambers of commerce, digital-ID vendors; CZ exposure: ties to CZ datovky/eGov interop; legislation in negotiation

title: Chips Act 2.0 — remaining gaps in advanced semiconductor manufacturing and AI chips
summary: Evaluation and revision of the Chips Act: manufacturing investment materialised but gaps persist in advanced nodes and AI chips. Proposal feedback open until 10 Sep 2026; 216 feedback items across the initiative.
notes: 216 total feedback; semiconductor industry, research orgs; CZ exposure: onsemi Roznov expansion, CZ chip design/packaging suppliers

title: Cloud and AI Development Act — EU gap in cloud and AI compute capacity
summary: The Act addresses the EU's shortfall in cloud/AI infrastructure capacity via R&I, industrial investment in sustainable data centres and easier permitting. Adopted proposal open for feedback until 9 Oct 2026; 464 feedback items accumulated across stages.
notes: 464 total feedback (27 on proposal); hyperscaler dependence is the stated problem; CZ exposure: CZ data-centre projects, AI startups needing compute, energy grid for DCs

title: Digital Fitness Check — cumulative digital-acquis burden on firms under review
summary: Fitness check evaluating whether the EU digital rulebook is coherent and proportionate as a whole, feeding the digital omnibus simplification. Closed 11 Mar 2026 with 293 feedback items (187 CFE + 106 OPC).
notes: 293 feedback; industry associations dominated; feeds digital omnibus (tracked separately as consult-digital-omnibus); CZ exposure: compliance burden on CZ SMEs/SaaS

title: Digital Networks Act — fragmented telecom regulation slows connectivity investment
summary: The DNA proposal tackles under-investment in fixed/wireless high-speed networks and fragmented telecom rules that hold back cloud and AI-ready connectivity. Adopted proposal is open for feedback until 7 Sep 2026; the initiative accumulated 550 feedback items across its stages.
notes: 550 total feedback (9 on adopted proposal so far); telcos, ISPs, tech industry; CZ exposure: CETIN/O2/T-Mobile/Vodafone market structure, spectrum and access regulation

title: Dual-Use Regulation evaluation — export controls under strain from tech and geopolitics
summary: Mandated evaluation of Regulation 2021/821 controlling exports of dual-use items, testing whether it still meets objectives amid technology and security shifts. OPC open until 15 Oct 2026; 19 feedback items.
notes: 17 OPC + 2 CFE feedback; exporters, defence-adjacent tech; CZ exposure: CZ defence/electronics exporters face licensing friction

title: EBA DGS package — deposit protection for client funds held by payment/e-money firms
summary: EBA consults on four DGSD2 mandates, led by RTS on deposit-guarantee payouts of client funds deposited by payment institutions, e-money firms and investment firms — an unresolved protection gap. All four consultations close 23 Oct 2026.
notes: Package of 4 open EBA consultations (client-funds payouts RTS, investment of DGS funds GL, information-exchange ITS, depositor-information ITS), all 23 Jul - 23 Oct 2026; CZ exposure: CZ payment/e-money fintechs safeguarding client funds at banks

title: EBA methodology for MiCA fines — how penalties on issuers/CASPs will be calculated
summary: EBA consults on the methodology for setting fines under MiCA for significant asset-referenced and e-money token issuers, defining enforcement exposure for the crypto sector. Closes 28 Sep 2026.
notes: Open 26 Jun - 28 Sep 2026; complements EC MiCA evaluation OPC; CZ exposure: CZ CASPs and stablecoin-adjacent firms face the enforcement regime

title: EIOPA IRRD valuation RTS — how failing insurers will be valued in resolution
summary: EIOPA consults on draft technical standards for valuation of insurers in recovery and resolution under the new IRRD (two parallel consultations covering valuations 1-3). Both close 20 Oct 2026.
notes: 2 open EIOPA consultations (RTS valuation 1&2 and valuation 3), 8 Jul - 20 Oct 2026; CZ exposure: CZ insurers (Generali CP, Kooperativa) enter IRRD resolution planning

title: Employers Sanctions Directive evaluation — sanctions fail to deter illegal employment
summary: Evaluation tests whether the directive penalising employers of irregularly staying third-country nationals remains fit for purpose. Feedback until 18 Sep 2026; 7 responses.
notes: 7 feedback; employers, labour inspectorates, migrant-rights NGOs; CZ exposure: CZ labour shortage draws irregular employment in construction/agriculture

title: ESAs technical advice on Taxonomy KPIs — sustainability disclosure metrics under simplification
summary: ESMA consulted on technical advice simplifying selected KPIs under the Taxonomy Disclosures Delegated Act after persistent complaints that the metrics are burdensome and low-value; closed 12 Aug 2026. EBA opened its parallel discussion paper on the same mandate on 12 Aug 2026.
notes: ESMA leg closed 12 Aug 2026 (window 1 Jul - 12 Aug); EBA discussion paper open from 12 Aug; part of omnibus sustainability simplification; CZ exposure: CZ banks/listed firms doing Taxonomy reporting

title: ETS2 financial compensation rules — double-counted carbon costs must be refunded to consumers
summary: Implementing act sets rules for compensating final fuel consumers where ETS2 carbon costs are double-counted or unintendedly covered. Feedback window closes 14 Aug 2026; 16 responses.
notes: 16 feedback; fuel suppliers, consumer bodies; CZ exposure: ETS2 heating/transport-fuel costs are a top CZ political issue for 2027 launch

title: Europol Regulation recast — mandate too weak for current organised-crime threat
summary: Proposal to reinforce Europol's operational role against serious and organised crime, expanding data and cooperation powers. Adopted proposal open for feedback until 9 Oct 2026; 54 feedback items across the initiative.
notes: 54 feedback; civil-liberties NGOs vs law-enforcement bodies; CZ exposure: moderate — policing cooperation

title: Grid connection network codes revision — connection rules lag storage and renewables
summary: Revision of the RfG/DCC network codes governing generator and demand connection requirements, needed for system security as renewables, storage and data centres connect. Draft delegated regulation feedback closes 25 Aug 2026; 19 responses.
notes: 19 feedback; TSOs/DSOs, renewables and storage industry; CZ exposure: CEPS connection queue, CZ solar/battery boom blocked on grid capacity

title: Horizon Europe 2028-2034 partnerships — fragmented instruments burden R&D consortia
summary: OPC on redesigning European partnerships (joint undertakings) for FP10, simplifying implementation modes into a portfolio approach. Open until 16 Oct 2026; the initiative has drawn 1,396 feedback items across stages (88 on the OPC so far).
notes: 1,396 total feedback — heavy research-community response; universities, industry consortia; CZ exposure: CZ participation in JUs (Clean Aviation, Chips JU)

title: Housing simplification package — EU rules add cost and delay to housing supply
summary: Based on mapping of EU legislation impacting housing supply and affordability, the package seeks regulatory simplification for the housing sector, including state-aid and implementation aspects. Call for evidence (impact assessment) open until 30 Sep 2026; 41 feedback items.
notes: 41 feedback; developers, municipalities, housing NGOs; CZ exposure: acute housing affordability crisis in Prague/Brno; first EU-level housing package

title: Individual learning accounts evaluation — adult training participation still too low
summary: Evaluation of the 2022 Council Recommendation on individual learning accounts, reviewing whether it raised adult learning participation and closed skills gaps. Feedback until 18 Sep 2026; 9 responses.
notes: 9 feedback; training providers, social partners; CZ exposure: CZ adult-learning participation below EU average, upskilling agenda

title: MiCA evaluation — how the EU crypto-assets framework performs in practice
summary: Mandated evaluation of the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation reviews implementation, supervision and gaps (Articles 140/142). OPC open until 30 Sep 2026 with 95 responses so far.
notes: 95 OPC responses; CASPs, exchanges, banks; CZ exposure: large CZ crypto scene (CNB licensing of CASPs ongoing in 2026)

title: PPWR producer register implementing rules — fragmented EPR registration/reporting across member states
summary: Implementing rules under the Packaging Regulation harmonise producer registers and producer reporting for packaging EPR, today fragmented across 27 national schemes. The draft implementing regulation drew 4,348 feedback items — extraordinary for a technical act — before the window closes 10 Sep 2026.
notes: 4,348 feedback on draft implementing regulation — heaviest technical-act response in scan; e-commerce sellers and SMEs facing 27x registration burden; CZ exposure: every CZ producer/e-shop selling packaged goods cross-border

title: Basic skills in school education — long-term decline in European pupils' fundamentals
summary: Initiative addresses the sustained decline in basic skills (literacy, numeracy, digital) and widening performance gaps across EU school systems. Call for evidence open until 8 Sep 2026 (73 feedback items across the linked education package).
notes: Joint CFE with Teachers Agenda and Quality Education 2040 roadmap (initiative 18873); CZ exposure: falling PISA trend in CZ basic skills

title: EU Teachers Agenda — teacher shortages from low attractiveness and workload
summary: Call for evidence on tackling teacher shortages driven by ageing workforce, low career attractiveness and workload, plus new AI-era skill demands. Open until 8 Sep 2026; 73 feedback items across the education package.
notes: 73 feedback on joint education-package CFE; teacher unions, ministries; CZ exposure: CZ regional teacher shortages, especially STEM

title: Territorial supply constraints — manufacturers block cross-border sourcing, inflating retail prices
summary: Large manufacturers prevent retailers from buying in one member state and reselling in another, fragmenting the single market and driving significant price differences for daily goods. OPC open until 29 Sep 2026; 137 feedback items so far.
notes: 137 feedback incl. 27 on OPC; retailers/wholesalers vs brand manufacturers; CZ exposure: very high — CZ pays more for identical branded groceries, a running Czech political issue

title: Revision of EU tobacco rules — outdated rules vs new products and digital marketing
summary: The EC consults on updating EU tobacco control rules that no longer match market developments, new nicotine products and digital marketing practices. The open public consultation drew 36,526 responses (118,694 feedback items across the initiative) before closing 14 Aug 2026.
notes: 36,526 OPC responses; 118,694 total feedback across all stages — largest open EC consultation of 2026; industry, health NGOs and citizens; CZ exposure: vape/nicotine retail and advertising rules

title: EU victims' rights strategy 2026-2030 — rights on paper not exercised in practice
summary: New strategy to make victims' rights effective in practice across member states, addressing emerging threats including online victimisation. OPC open until 5 Nov 2026; call-for-evidence stage drew 22 responses.
notes: 22 CFE feedback, OPC just opened 13 Aug 2026; justice NGOs, member states; CZ exposure: moderate — transposition gaps

title: EU position for WRC-27 — spectrum decisions will shape 6G and satellite access
summary: Council decision setting the Union position for the ITU World Radiocommunication Conference 2027, covering spectrum allocation stakes for mobile, satellite and scientific use. Call for evidence until 11 Sep 2026; 5 responses.
notes: 5 feedback; telcos, satellite operators; CZ exposure: CTU spectrum roadmap, 6G band decisions

title: Mail never reaches people registered at town halls — 1,300+ items found stuck at a third of checked offices
summary: A 2025 nationwide CTU inspection of postal delivery to people whose registered residence is a municipal office (ohlasovna) found undelivered letters and postal money orders lying at roughly a third of 77 randomly checked town halls - over 1,300 items - now subject to administrative proceedings. The failure hits the debt-enforcement population hardest, since missed official mail drives default judgments.
notes: VZ CTU 2025: 'Ze 77 nahodne vybranych obecnich a mestskych uradu byly na zhruba tretine nalezeny dopisy nebo postovni poukazy'; 'pochybeni se tykala vice nez 1 300 zasilek'; navazujici spravni rizeni. Vazba: ngo-mapa-zadluzeni (596k osob v exekuci, doruceni fikci).

title: Telco billing disputes at industrial scale — 35,509 subscriber disputes handled by CTU in 2025
summary: The Czech Telecommunication Office's 2025 annual report shows it handled 35,509 subscriber disputes (21,685 newly opened, 13,824 carried over) and issued 23,887 decisions in one year, plus 2,828 complaints about e-communications services - mostly subscriber contracts and billing - with marketing-call complaints rising. Dispute resolution between operators and customers remains a mass administrative process.
notes: VZ CTU 2025: 'rozhodovali celkem 35 509 ucastnickych sporu, z toho ... prevedeno 13 824 ... nove zahajeno 21 685'; 23 887 rozhodnuti; 2 828 stiznosti na sluzby el. komunikaci; 942 dotazu; posta: 757 pisemnych stiznosti + 174 dotazu.

title: Clean mobility — 0 charging stations delivered from OPD3, 3 AFIR targets unmet, CZ 24th in EU
money_note: Charging infrastructure delivery gap; 54,864 BEVs = 1.2% of fleet (30.9.2025)
summary: NKU audit 25/11 found clean-mobility rollout lagging: the 2021-2027 transport programme had delivered zero public charging stations by audit close, three AFIR coverage targets are unmet, and with 54,864 battery EVs (1.2% of the fleet) CZ ranks 24th in the EU on electromobility. Safety rules for charging and for parking gas-fueled cars in shared garages are still not finalized, blocking installations in apartment buildings.
notes: KZ 25/11; 0 stanic z OPD 2021-2027; 3 cile AFIR neplneny; 54 864 BEV = 1,2 % parku; 24. misto v EU; 1 318 z 3 258 stanic z OPD 2014-2020 (41 %); chybi pravidla pro dobijeni v hromadnych garazich.

title: Digital and Information Agency — 114M CZK misstatements in 2025 accounts; 5.2bn corrected after NKU alert
money_note: Misstatements 114.33M CZK in DIA 2025 financial statements; further 5,198M CZK of defects fixed pre-closing after NKU warning
summary: NKU audit 25/17 (published 10 Aug 2026) found the Digital and Information Agency — the body running Czech state digitalization — misstated its 2025 balance sheet by 114.33M CZK by keeping in-use intangible assets parked as unfinished, and only fixed another 5.2bn CZK of bookkeeping defects after NKU flagged them mid-audit. NKU rated the affected balance-sheet accounts unreliable.
notes: KZ 25/17; nespravnosti 114,33 mil. Kc (ucet 041 vs 01x); dalsich 5 198 mil. Kc opraveno po upozorneni NKU; vykaz FIN bez vyznamnych vad.

title: Transport R&D programme — 1.74bn CZK drawn with no indicators to show real-world benefit
money_note: DOPRAVA 2020+ contracted 1,799M CZK, drawn 1,740.9M CZK
summary: NKU audit 24/30 found the DOPRAVA 2020+ applied-research programme (1.74bn CZK drawn) has no monitoring indicators or baseline/target values for its goals and impacts, no interim evaluation of whether results are used in practice, and evaluation timed so real benefits cannot be known. Some funded projects' results are not translating into practice despite formal delivery.
notes: KZ 24/30; 1 950 mil. plan, 1 799,34 mil. smlouvy, 1 740,93 mil. cerpano; zadne monitorovaci indikatory dopadu; MD bez prubezneho hodnoceni.

title: Cross-border e-commerce VAT — customs found value discrepancies in 61% of checked parcels
money_note: 1.28bn EUR VAT received via OSS/IOSS 2021-2024; 98M EUR of payments once sat unmatched to tax returns
summary: NKU audit 25/01 found the Financial Administration lacks reliable data to verify VAT declared under the EU e-commerce regime, and the Customs Administration found undervaluation in 61% of inspected low-value parcels. In Nov 2022 unmatched VAT payments exceeded 98M EUR; 461k EUR of payment allocations were still unresolved in April 2025.
notes: KZ 25/01 (zverejneno ve Vestniku NKU 1.12.2025); '61 % zkontrolovanych zasilek' undervalued; DPH prijata 2021-2024 cca 1,280 mld. eur; FU JMK nevyjasnene rozpisy 461 tis. eur (24.4.2025), v 11/2022 pres 98 mil. eur neprirazeno.

title: Digital technical maps — 4.8bn CZK spent, >50% of infrastructure owners never filed mandatory data
money_note: 2.89bn CZK to regions + 1.68bn NPO follow-ups + 247M CUZK on DMVS
summary: NKU audit 24/07 found that despite ~4.8bn CZK spent, the digital technical maps that were to be the authoritative source on utilities and transport infrastructure from 1 July 2024 are incomplete and unreliable: over 50% of identified infrastructure owners had not filed legally required data and over 50% of sampled objects had unreliable records. Construction-permitting digitalization depends on this layer.
notes: KZ 24/07; ZAKLADNI FAKTA: 2,89 mld. + 247 mil. + 1,68 mld. Kc; 'Pres 50 % vlastniku infrastruktury nezaneslo do DTM zakonem pozadovane udaje'; 'pres 50 % objektu kontrolovaneho vzorku' nespolehlive.

title: eRecept — SMS-first delivery doubled costs 2020-2024; SUKL procurement breaches in 7 of 13 ICT tenders
money_note: SMS delivery costs of eRecept identifiers more than doubled 2020->2024; 347M CZK spend audited
summary: NKU audit 24/25 found SUKL repeatedly breached procurement law (transparency violations in 7 of 13 audited ICT tenders, missing audit trail for value estimates; unlawful direct award of catering during CZ PRES 2022) and that eRecept identifier delivery relies dominantly on SMS, more than doubling delivery costs between 2020 and 2024 because cheaper channels (app, email, ID card) are underused.
notes: KZ 24/25; 7/13 ICT zakazek poruseni transparentnosti; vydaje na SMS 2020->2024 vice nez dvojnasobne; kontrolovano 347 mil. Kc.

title: e-Sbirka/e-Legislativa — 6 years late, budget doubled to 903M CZK, 581M paid on unlawful amendments
money_note: Project budget grew 482M -> 903M CZK; 108.5M CZK non-economical; 581M CZK paid under contract amended in breach of procurement law
summary: NKU audit 24/04 concluded the Interior Ministry failed at managing the e-Sbirka/e-Legislativa legal-information system: delivery stretched from 3 to 9 years, the budget nearly doubled to 903M CZK, and 581M CZK was paid under unlawfully amended contracts. The launched e-Sbirka part does not deliver key promised benefits such as a clear view of law in force at a given time.
notes: KZ 24/04; puvodne 482 mil. -> 903 mil. Kc; zpozdeni 6 let (dokonceni az 2026); 108,5 mil. nehospodarne; 581 mil. neopravnene (dodatky v rozporu se ZZVZ); 278,6 mil. na e-Sbirku se snizenou ucelnosti.

title: ETCS train protection — 1.95bn CZK for 622 km with no speed/capacity gains; 48.8bn expansion ahead
money_note: 1.95bn CZK spent on trackside ETCS (622 km); planned expansion to ~5,000 km by 2033 calculated at 48.8bn CZK; future 10M CZK/km vs 3M/km to date
summary: NKU audit 25/05 found ETCS exclusive operation covers 622 km (40% of the CZ TEN-T core) for 1.95bn CZK but delivers only the safety function — promised faster operation and higher track capacity did not materialize, reducing efficiency of the spend. Expansion to ~5,000 km of mostly regional lines by 2033 is costed at 48.8bn CZK with per-km costs expected at 10M CZK versus 3M so far, and no variant analysis is done per line.
notes: KZ 25/05; 622 km vyhradni provoz od 2/2025; 1,95 mld. Kc; prumer 3 mil. Kc/km; dalsi TEN-T ~9 mld.; rozsireni na 5 000 km za 48,8 mld. Kc do 2033.

title: University-hospital investment — 2bn CZK granted with zero on-site controls; VFN urgent care unbuilt after 14 years
money_note: 2bn CZK 2016-2022 from programme 135 01; overspend 295M CZK above approved financing
summary: NKU audit 24/09 found the Health Ministry distributed 2bn CZK for university-hospital infrastructure without collecting data on building conditions, without integrated goals and without performing a single on-site public-finance control at recipients; a third of investment actions were registered only near programme end and spending exceeded the approved envelope by 295M CZK. The central urgent-care ward at Prague's VFN remained unbuilt 14 years on.
notes: KZ 24/09; 2 mld. Kc bez jedine verejnospravni kontroly; prekroceni 295 mil.; 3 z 8 pristroju nevyuzivane deklarovane; 'Centralni urgentni prijem ve VFN ani po 14 letech nebyl vybudovan'.

title: Research agencies — 30bn CZK in grants; citations below half the EU average, no patent growth
money_note: GACR+TACR grants 2021-2023 nearly 30bn CZK; GACR redistributes >4bn CZK/year
summary: NKU audit 24/17 found the effectiveness of ~30bn CZK in competitive research funding (2021-2023) is dragged by defects flagged already in 2017: citation impact of basic research remains below half the European average, TACR did not expand public-private cooperation or patent counts, and the 2018 GACR-TACR cooperation memorandum produced no concrete outputs. GACR still has not launched its planned call for urgent, strategically oriented basic research.
notes: KZ 24/17; ~30 mld. Kc 2021-2023; citovanost < 1/2 evropskeho prumeru; memorandum 2018 bez vystupu; orientovany zakladni vyzkum nevyhlasen.

title: Justice debt collection — 7.65bn CZK owed, courts recovered ~8%, customs ~9%
money_note: Tax-type justice receivables under enforcement in 2023: 7.65bn CZK; court fees income 1.38bn CZK (2024)
summary: NKU audit 24/31 found courts collected justice receivables (fines, monetary penalties, court fees, criminal-proceedings costs) with only ~8% success in 2021-2023, and the Customs Administration that took over from 2024 achieves ~9%, albeit at lower cost. The reform's stated goal of more frequent monetary penalties has not materialized.
notes: KZ 24/31; vymahane danove justicni pohledavky 7,65 mld. Kc (2023); uspesnost soudu cca 8 %, CS CR 9 %; soudni poplatky 1,38 mld. Kc prijmu 2024.

title: Forestry support — 32.7bn CZK without target state; climate-adaptation programme cancelled
money_note: 32.7bn CZK on forestry support 2014-2024
summary: NKU audit 24/16 found 32.7bn CZK of forestry support flowed without MZe defining a target state or evaluating progress against the 2035 forestry policy; MZe declined available EU financing for the forest-ecosystem adaptation programme, then cancelled the nationally funded programme in budget cuts, putting the climate-adaptation goal at risk. The 2014-2020 afforestation target was missed.
notes: KZ 24/16; 32,7 mld. Kc 2014-2024; MZe bez ciloveho stavu; program adaptace lesnich ekosystemu zrusen (nevyuzito EU financovani); cil zalesnovani PRV nesplnen.

title: Police aviation — no new helicopters since 2017 plans, hangar in emergency state ~20 years, 24/7 SAR limited
money_note: 1,343.7M CZK spent on LS PCR 2021-2025; 97% operations, 3% investment
summary: NKU audit 25/12 found the Interior Ministry failed to make priority investments in the Police Aviation Service: planned helicopter purchases stalled since 2017 and the main Prague hangar has been in an officially emergency state for nearly 20 years. As a result the service cannot guarantee full round-the-clock search-and-rescue capacity, night operations at planned scale, or effective aerial firefighting.
notes: KZ 25/12; 1 343,7 mil. Kc 2021-2025 (97 % provoz); vrtulniky neporizeny (ukol od 2017), hangar havarijni ~20 let (od 2010); omezene 24h SAR a nocni lety.

title: Local-road subsidies — 4.72bn CZK spread with negligible benefit and no outcome tracking
money_note: 4.72bn CZK distributed 2019-2025 from Podpora rozvoje regionu
summary: NKU audit 25/04 found MMR's 4.72bn CZK local-road renovation subsidy was not spent purposefully: benefits to traffic, quality of life or attractiveness were insignificant, some defects survived the renovations, and 6 of 20 audited recipients breached grant terms. MMR does not track whether the intervention achieves anything and closes project files years late.
notes: KZ 25/04; 4 722 mil. Kc 2019-2025; 'prinos ... byl nevyznamny'; 6/20 projektu poruseni rozpoctove kazne; MMR nevyhodnocuje prinosy.

title: Modernization Fund RES+ — 95% of allocation locked into solar only; 2030 RES target far off track
money_note: 105.6bn CZK received from EIB by 30.6.2024, 32.8bn paid out; 73bn committed to PV projects
summary: NKU audit 24/06 found the Modernization Fund's RES+ programme supported exclusively photovoltaics — 73bn CZK (95% of the estimated allocation to 2030) is committed to PV, leaving no room for other renewables — while the CZ 2030 target of a 30% renewables share compares with 18.59% reached in 2023. Wind (1.5 GW needed) has no support route from the fund.
notes: KZ 24/06; SFZP prijal 105,6 mld. Kc, vyplatil 32,8 mld.; RES+ 12,7 mld. vyplaceno; 'jine druhy zarizeni na vyrobu energie z OZE ani nebude mozne z MdF podporit' — 73 mld. obhajeno u EIB na FVE = 95 % alokace RES+ do 2030; cil 30 % OZE vs 18,59 % (2023).

title: Illegal employment enforcement — only 9.3% of 3,019 referrals investigated, ~1M CZK fiscal effect
money_note: Fiscal impact of tax follow-up on referrals: ~1M CZK over 2021-2023; 2,408 final labour-inspection fines 2019-2024
summary: NKU audit 24/14 found the tax administration checked only 9.3% of 3,019 illegal-employment referrals from labour inspection and customs (2021-2023), with a fiscal impact of about 1M CZK. No authority is legally competent to recover social-insurance contributions from employers fined for illegal employment because the EU Sanctions Directive was insufficiently transposed.
notes: KZ 24/14; SUIP/GRC podnetu 3,019, FS CR zkontrolovala 9,3 %; CSSZ 2019-2024 obdrzela 2,408 pravomocnych pokut; chybi kompetence domerit pojistne (Sankcni smernice 2009/52/ES).

title: Motorway rest areas — zero of 18 priority sites built; 1,898 truck parking spots missing
money_note: 441M CZK spent 2018-2024 preparing 74 rest areas; 3.8M CZK on flawed siting studies
summary: NKU audit 24/18 found that of 18 rest areas RSD marked most-needed for delivery by 2023, none was built; 441M CZK went into preparation while at end-2024 motorways lacked 1,898 truck parking spots (vs a 2017 government target of 1,500 new spots by 2023, of which only 407 materialized). Truckers legally required to take rest breaks park dangerously, and the promised parking-availability/reservation system due by 2020 still does not exist.
notes: KZ 24/18; 0/18 nejpotrebnejsich odpocivek; 441 mil. Kc na pripravu; chybi 1 898 mist pro kamiony (konec 2024); cil 1 500 mist do 2023 -> 407; rezervacni system slibeny do 2020 neexistuje.

title: Pedestrian infrastructure subsidies — 9.5bn CZK; 17 of 23 audited projects not purposeful
money_note: 9,536M CZK of state+EU support to municipalities 2014-2023
summary: NKU audit 24/01 found support for building and renovating pavements and pedestrian routes (9.5bn CZK over 2014-2023) was largely not spent purposefully: ministries do not know what overall outcomes they want or achieved, support was not steered where most useful, and 17 of 23 audited projects were assessed as non-purposeful or only partly purposeful (10 also uneconomical). NKU recommends redesigning the whole support system.
notes: KZ 24/01; 9 536 mil. Kc 2014-2023; vzorek 23 projektu/138 mil.; 17/23 neucelne ci omezene ucelne, 10 nehospodarne.

title: Land consolidation — 50 more years and 145bn CZK needed at current pace; 75% of cadastres unfinished
money_note: 36.2bn CZK spent 1991-2023; NKU estimates >=144.9bn CZK needed to finish
summary: NKU audit 23/31 found complex land consolidations — key for farming access, erosion and drought resilience — are finished in only 24.9% of cadastral areas after 33 years and 36.2bn CZK; completing the remaining 9,186 areas would need at least 144.9bn CZK and ~50 years at the current pace. The Agriculture Ministry does not track effectiveness and has no cost estimate of its own.
notes: KZ 23/31; dokonceno 3 046 KU = 24,9 %; zbyvá 9 186 KU; 36,2 mld. Kc 1991-2023; odhad NKU min. 144,9 mld.; 'nejmene 50 let'.

title: Flood protection and water retention — 7.1bn CZK; 3 of 8 programmes missed retention targets
money_note: 7.1bn CZK spent 2020-2024, of which ~3bn from NPO
summary: NKU audit 25/06 found landscape water retention is not being sufficiently secured: of eight subsidy programmes three failed their retention goals, one missed 10 of 15 indicator targets, and MZe repeatedly lowered target values to make programmes look achieved. The 2030 strategy has no outcome indicators, so 7.1bn CZK of spending cannot be linked to actual flood-prevention effect.
notes: KZ 25/06; 7,1 mld. Kc 2020-2024 (3 mld. NPO); program 129 390 nedosahl 10 z 15 ukazatelu; MZe 'opakovane snizovalo cilove hodnoty ukazatelu'.

title: REACT-EU hospital resilience — 18.6bn CZK rushed into devices; 12 of 27 checked units underused
money_note: 18.6bn CZK REACT-EU health projects; 41.1M CZK of sampled devices significantly underused
summary: NKU audit 25/07 found 18.6bn CZK of REACT-EU 'hospital resilience' funding was spent mostly on devices bought under time pressure at 100% subsidy, with need not verified (not at all below 5M CZK); 12 of 27 audited devices worth 41.1M CZK were used far less than is usual, one not at all after two years. The urgent-admissions network the support was tied to will not be complete before 2029, when much equipment will be obsolete.
notes: KZ 25/07; 18,6 mld. Kc; dotace 100 %; 12/27 pristroju za 41,1 mil. Kc vyrazne malo vyuzivanych; 3 pristroje <10 vykonu/rok; sit urgentnich prijmu dokoncena nejdrive 2029.

title: School-system governance projects — 506.8M CZK without effect on education quality; PISA stagnates
money_note: 3,519.5M CZK earmarked 2019-2024 for evaluation/governance projects; 506.8M on governance projects ruled non-purposeful
summary: NKU audit 25/02 found systemic projects for managing regional schooling (506.8M CZK) did not meet goals of improving education quality or pupil outcomes — PISA and CSI results stagnate or decline — and the action plans they produced are widely seen by schools as formal documents with no real impact. MSMT keeps funding methodical-support projects with low uptake and did not evaluate its long-term education strategy goals as required by law.
notes: KZ 25/02; 3 519,5 mil. Kc celkem; 506,8 mil. neucelne; IS vzdelavani 1,3 mil. nehospodarne; PISA stagnace/pokles; akcni plany 'formalni dokumenty bez realneho dopadu'.

title: Elite-sport centres — 3.4bn CZK spent while flagship facilities were never built
money_note: OLYMP CS MV 1,352.4M + DUKLA 2,089.3M CZK 2019-2023
summary: NKU audit 24/08 found the two ministerial elite-sport centres spent 3.4bn CZK (2019-2023) with instances of non-purposeful and uneconomical purchases, while planned flagship infrastructure — the Vera Caslavska National Training Centre and completion of the Juliska complex — was never delivered in 2016-2024 and modernization spending fell, contrary to the SPORT 2025 concept.
notes: KZ 24/08; 1 352,4 + 2 089,3 mil. Kc; MV zrealizovalo 38 % investicnich akci podprogramu; NTC Very Caslavske nevybudovano; Juliska nedokoncena.

title: Rainwater adaptation — only 3% of municipalities reached; green roofs got 1% of NZU money
money_note: 1.84bn CZK 2021-2025 via OPZP21+/NPO; dest'ovka+green roofs got 167.73M of 15.71bn CZK NZU
summary: NKU audit 25/08 found rainwater-management support reached just 182 municipalities (3% of all CZ municipalities) with 1.59bn CZK, used incomparable indicators across programmes so results cannot be assessed, and within Nova zelena usporam only 167.73M CZK of 15.71bn went to rain-capture and green roofs as applicants preferred heat pumps and PV. CZ visibly lags Austria and Germany in green-roof development.
notes: KZ 25/08; 1,84 mld. Kc; 182 obci = 3 % obci CR; NZU: 167,73 mil. z 15,71 mld.; MZP studie 2019 bez cilu, milniku a odpovednosti.

title: Civil-service professionalization — 873.5M CZK with limited effect; 640M ISoSS lacks analytics
money_note: 873.5M CZK on professionalization; ISoSS system up to 640M CZK with reduced effectiveness; 22.6M CZK on exam digitalization ruled uneconomical
summary: NKU audit 24/28 found 873.5M CZK spent on professionalizing the civil service had limited impact: most offices did not adopt the required quality-management minimum, training and the civil-service exam were not digitalized, and the 640M CZK ISoSS staff-registry cannot produce the data needed to manage the service, forcing extra spending on questionnaires. The civil-service law was amended 45 times since 2014 and its 2024 overhaul again skipped impact assessment via exemption.
notes: KZ 24/28; 873,5 mil. Kc; PROAK 96,3 mil. omezeny dopad; 22,6 mil. nehospodarne; ISoSS az 640 mil. se snizenou efektivnosti; ZoSS novelizovan 45x; vyjimka z RIA.

title: Labour Office — 16% of personnel costs on late benefit processing; digitalization didn't speed up work
money_note: 1.4bn CZK spent on EFES+PIPS efficiency projects 2016-2023; 34.7M CZK ruled non-purposeful; 5.1bn CZK property audited
summary: NKU audit 24/32 found the Czech Labour Office spent up to 16% of personnel costs inefficiently administering non-insurance social benefits it failed to process within legal deadlines, and that digitalization increased comfort for a third of clients but did not speed up staff work. Efficiency projects worth 1.4bn CZK produced only temporary benefits and 14 years after its creation the office still lacks unified property procedures.
notes: KZ 24/32; 'az 16 % osobnich nakladu na administraci zadosti o nepojistne socialni davky, ktere nevyridil v zakonne lhute'; digitalizace 'k urychleni prace zamestnancu dosud neprispela'; EFES+PIPS 1,4 mld. Kc; 34,7 mil. Kc neucelne.

title: Energy-efficiency subsidies — 26.4bn CZK delivered only 1% consumption saving in industry and services
money_note: 26.4bn CZK paid from OP PIK/OP TAK/NPO by 1.5.2025; 13.9bn on OP PIK savings programme alone
summary: NKU audit 24/24 found that 26.4bn CZK of MPO energy-efficiency and renewables support had negligible effect: the OP PIK savings programme achieved 4.6 PJ against a 51.5 PJ national 2020 target (6% of plan), equal to a 1% saving of final energy consumption in industry and services. OP TAK brought no increase in installed RES capacity by end-2024 and the NPO state-buildings scheme attracts almost no applicants due to badly set conditions.
notes: KZ 24/24; proplaceno 26,4 mld. Kc; uspora 1 % spotreby; 2020 cil 51,5 PJ vs dosazeno 3,1 PJ (6 %); 13,9 mld. -> 4,6 PJ; riziko nesplneni cile snizeni energeticke narocnosti budov OSS.

title: Visa & consular IT — five replacement systems all delayed with no completion date; passport-agenda IT costs up 22x
money_note: 683M CZK spent 2016-2025 on consular IT support; 732M planned for successor systems; 5.5bn CZK visa-fee income in MZV chapter 2016-2024
summary: NKU audit 24/26 found visa and consular services run on obsolete systems requiring manual re-typing of data between systems and courier shipping of paper documents from abroad, while all five replacement IT projects of MZV and MV are delayed with no determinable completion date. Annual MZV spend on passport-agenda IT support jumped 22-fold between 2022 and 2024 (1.16M to 25.9M CZK) with no change in the agenda.
notes: KZ 24/26; 683 mil. Kc 2016-2025; 732 mil. planovano; prijmy z viz 5 502 mil. Kc; 'rucni kopirovani udaju', 'komercni kuryrni sluzba'; naklady na pasy 22x (1,16 -> 25,9 mil. Kc/rok).

title: High-speed rail — 737bn CZK project with no financing source; 5.6bn already spent on preparation
money_note: Investment need >=737bn CZK; 5.6bn CZK spent on preparation so far
summary: NKU audit 25/09 concluded high-speed rail construction is not prepared for effective delivery: minimum cost is 737bn CZK yet financing sources were undetermined at audit close, the German treaty for the Krusnohorsky tunnel unratified, and several routes missing from land-use plans. Expected social benefits used to justify the project are not credibly demonstrated and early construction sections cost more per km than prior modernizations.
notes: KZ 25/09; 'minimalne 737 mld. Kc'; 5,6 mld. vynalozeno na pripravu; zdroje financovani neurceny; smlouva s SRN neratifikovana; trasy chybi v uzemnich planech.

title: Army training facilities — 1.8bn CZK invested yet capacity and simulators still inadequate
money_note: ~1.8bn CZK invested 2019-2024 in training facilities; 1,441.5M audited
summary: NKU audit 24/12 found that despite ~1.8bn CZK invested since 2019, army training facilities do not match current needs: modern simulators are lacking and not NATO-interconnected, delayed garage construction in Praslavice/Bucovice forces new combat vehicles to be housed in Vyskov with crews commuting tens of kilometres, and missed recruitment targets risk overloading training capacity during any rapid intake.
notes: KZ 24/12; temer 1,8 mld. Kc 2019-2024; zpozdeni garazi -> vozidla docasne ve Vyskove; chybi simulatory a NATO propojeni; roztristeny sber dat o vycviku.

title: Social services for autism — systemic unavailability now before the Constitutional Court
summary: The ombudsman and child ombudsman jointly told the Constitutional Court (case II. US 215/26) that unavailability of social services for a young autistic person with high-support needs reflects a chain of systemic failures, not an individual lapse. Social services and disability support made up 21% of the 804 submissions in the 2026 inventory, which flags shortage of community services for people with autism as a recurring theme; after earlier ombudsman recommendations MPSV issued a service-availability methodology and VZP first published a list of special dental offices.
notes: Q2 2026 report A.3.2 (ESO 14540): ustavni stiznost II. US 215/26 - 'retezec systemovych' nedostatku; inventory 24.3.2026: socialni sluzby/pomoc 21 % z 804; 'nedostatek podpurnych sluzeb ... obzvlaste pro lidi s PAS'; VZP seznam specialnich ordinaci poprve zverejnen.

title: Building accessibility enforcement — 97% of exemption requests granted, 9% of authorities ever inspect
summary: Ombudsman research (2023, 239 of 280 municipal building authorities responding) found authorities denied only 10 of 305 requests (3%) for exemptions from the barrier-free construction decree, fewer than one in ten (9%) ever used a supervisory measure, and 29% of appellate building authorities never assessed accessibility at all. Completed buildings are rarely checked for actual accessibility, hollowing out the CRPD-based rules.
notes: Vyzkumna zprava 2023 (sp. zn. 3822/2021/VOP, c.j. KVOP-33644/2023): 305 zadosti o vyjimku, 10 zamitnuto (3 %); 19 uradu (9 %) alespon jedno dozorove opatreni; 29 % odvolacich uradu bezbarierovost vubec neposuzovalo; MHMP 360 z 652 pripadu (55 %). Restated in the 2026-03-24 systemic-problem inventory ('v 94 % pripadu vyjimku povoli').

title: Deinstitutionalization stalled — community-housing build-out fell ~80%, institutions count unchanged since 2007
summary: Ombudsman research (2023) found deinstitutionalization of disability care has stalled: 126 new community-housing (CHB) facilities were created in 2007-2015 but only 26 in 2016-2022 (a ~80% slowdown), while the number of institutional DOZP facilities was 208 in 2022 versus 205 in 2007. No region reported having transformed all facilities and only 11 regional development plans target community services by concrete criteria.
notes: Vyzkum 2023 (sp. zn. 27/2022/OZP, c.j. KVOP-12222/2024): CHB 126 novych 2007-2015 vs 26 v 2016-2022 ('zpomalil o temer ctyri petiny'); DOZP 205 (2007) -> 208 (2022); 'zadny kraj ... transformovana vsechna zarizeni'; pouze 11 SPRSS cili na komunitni sluzby; navazujici analyza + doporuceni slibeny na pul roku 2026 (inventory 24.3.2026).

title: Children's homes in unsuitable historic buildings — region resists transforming its 17 facilities
money_note: MSK region cited ~200M CZK already invested in children's homes as reason against relocation
summary: The ombudsman's visit to the Velke Heraltice children's home housed in a listed baroque castle found heritage rules make family-like living units impossible; the Moravian-Silesian region initially refused a relocation, citing ~200M CZK of past investment and no plan to transform any of its 17 children's homes without a change in the institutional-care law, before agreeing to prepare a transformation plan. The case documents the building-stock lock-in of residential child care.
notes: Q2 2026 report A.6.3 (sp. zn. 41/2024/NZ, ESO 14448): navsteva 1/2025; 'investice ... priblizne 200 milionu Kc'; 'neplanuje plosnou transformaci vsech 17 zarizeni'; kraj po jednani prislibil transformacni plan.

title: New child ombudsman — 595 submissions in Q2 2026, 65 directly from children, first court intervention
summary: In its first year the child ombudsman institution received 595 submissions in Q2 2026 (93% within mandate): 296 on child-protection authorities, 124 on schools, 27 on children's facilities, 26 on healthcare; 65 came directly from children. The office got 9 requests to enter court proceedings on child care and used this new power for the first time, evidencing unmet demand for child-rights advocacy.
notes: Q2 2026 report B.1 (c.j. KVOP-40911/2026): 595 podnetu, 15 setreni z vlastni iniciativy, pusobnost 93 %; struktura 296/124/27/26; 65 primo od deti; 9 zadosti o vstup do rizeni, poprve vyuzito; Martin Benes zvolen ochrancem prav deti (inventory 3/2026).

title: Mandatory digitalization without offline alternatives — ombudsman: absence of non-digital route can be discrimination
summary: In the 2026 systemic-topic inventory, digital exclusion dominated the equality area (15% of 804 submissions): mandatory digital-only public services, differential pricing for digital vs non-digital access (tickets, loyalty schemes), and inaccessibility for people under guardianship. The ombudsman's standing position is that discrimination can arise wherever no non-electronic or cash alternative accessible to non-users of technology exists.
notes: Inventory 24.3.2026: rovnost/netolerance 15 % z 804 podnetu; 'k diskriminaci muze dojit, pokud nebude existovat i jine nez elektronicke ci bezhotovostni reseni'; tyka se jizdenek, vstupenek, vernostnich programu retezcu; nedostupnost pro osoby omezene ve svepravnosti.

title: OSPOD child-protection casework — top complaint stream: 300+ ombudsman inquiries a year
summary: The ombudsman's 2026 systemic-problem inventory (804 public submissions) put family and child care first with 22% of submissions, dominated by complaints about OSPOD child-protection authorities; the office investigates over 300 individual OSPOD complaints a year. In Q2 2026 alone, 296 of the child ombudsman's 595 submissions concerned child-protection authorities' conduct in parental disputes and care failures.
notes: Inventory 24.3.2026: 'Rocne jich vyridime vice nez 300' (OSPOD podnetu); rodina a pece o deti 22 % z 804 podnetu. Q2 2026 report B.1: 296 z 595 podnetu detskeho ombudsmana = OSPOD oblast. MPSV metodika kontaktu s uveznenymi rodici vydana 2025 po doporuceni.

title: Temporary foster care — 726 case files show missing records and 9+ month delays finding permanent families
summary: Ombudsman research analyzed 726 files of children in temporary foster care (PPPD) across all regional authorities and found systematic record-keeping failures - missing inter-regional cooperation records, suitability notices and court decisions. All regions except two waited nine months or more in at least one case before asking other regions to find a child a permanent foster or adoptive family (Usti region: 15 such cases, 6 over a year), prolonging children's stays in what should be short-term care.
notes: Vyzkumna zprava 2022 (sp. zn. 6324/2021/VOP, c.j. KVOP-48556/2022): 726 spisu deti v PPPD (sber 28.4.-5.10.2021); navazuje na zpravu 2226/2020/VOP (21.9.2021, ESO 9872) o pochybenich kraju pri vyhledavani pestounu a osvojitelu; restated in inventory 24.3.2026.

title: Legal capacity — courts choose radical restriction over supported decision-making in 78% of cases
summary: In a submission to the UN independent expert (reported in the ombudsman's Q2 2026 report), the ombudsman documented that Czech courts opt for radical restriction of legal capacity instead of modern supportive measures in 78% of cases, and that residential care facilities practice blanket locking of clients and undocumented use of restraints. He urges immediate managed deinstitutionalization of long-term care and oversight of private guardians.
notes: Q2 2026 report (c.j. KVOP-40911/2026), section A.4.3: 'praxi soudu, ktere v 78 % pripadu voli radikalni omezeni svepravnosti namisto modernich podpurnych opatreni'; 'plosne zamykani osob, pouzivani omezovacich prostredku bez radne dokumentace'.

title: Gulf-conflict shock — 86% of Czech firms feel impacts; 67% cite energy prices, 40% expect investment cuts
summary: A Svaz prumyslu a dopravy member survey (8 Apr 2026) found 86% of Czech companies already feel Persian Gulf conflict impacts: higher energy prices (67%), input and raw-material costs (63%) and transport/logistics (53%), with a third reporting supply-chain disruption. 80% pass costs on to customers, 71% cut costs, and 40% expect negative investment effects; firms want excise (57%) or VAT (31%) cuts on fuel.
notes: SPCR pruzkum 8.4.2026: dopady 86 % firem; energie 67 %, vstupy/suroviny 63 %, doprava/logistika 53 %; treti narusene dodavatelske retezce; 80 % prenasi ceny, 71 % setri; 40 % negativni dopad na investice; pozadavky: spotrebni dan 57 %, DPH 31 %.

title: Psychiatric-drug shortages — 403 nervous-system products interrupted, incl. antipsychotics and antidepressants
summary: The largest block of current Czech drug-supply interruptions is nervous-system medication: 403 presentations interrupted as of 15 Aug 2026, including depot antipsychotics (Moditen Depot, Prosulpin) and antidepressants (sertraline, citalopram, clomipramine). This collides with the ombudsman-documented shortage of psychiatric care capacity, compounding continuity-of-treatment risk for psychiatric patients.
notes: MR dataset 15.08.2026: ATC N = 403 z 1,537; priklady MODITEN DEPOT, PROSULPIN, ZYLORAM (citalopram), SERLIFT (sertralin), ANAFRANIL SR (klomipramin); vazba na ombud zjisteni nedostupnosti psychiatru (inventory 2026).

title: Drug supply — 1,537 medicine presentations interrupted right now; a third with no promised return date
summary: SUKL's open supply-notification register shows 1,537 medicine presentations (454 distinct ATC codes) with supply currently interrupted as of 15 Aug 2026: nervous system 403, blood 201, cardiovascular 184, alimentary/metabolism 108, oncology/immunology 95, anti-infectives 86. 507 of them have no promised resumption date and manufacturers filed 2,069 new interruption notices in 2025 plus 1,330 more by mid-August 2026; leading stated cause is manufacturing problems (647).
notes: opendata.sukl.cz MR dataset, validity 15.08.2026; POSLEDNI_PLATNE_HLASENI=ANO & TYP=preruseni -> 1,537; ATC-1 rozpad N=403,V=203,B=201,C=184,A=108,L=95,J=86,G=69,M=62,R=40,H=31,D=30,S=24; bez TERMIN_OBNOVENI: 507; duvody: vyrobni 647, obchodni/marketingove 241, kapacitni/distribucni 81.

title: Market exits — 767 permanent supply terminations notified in 2025, another 474 by mid-2026
summary: Beyond temporary outages, manufacturers permanently terminated supply of 767 medicine presentations in 2025 and another 474 by mid-August 2026 per SUKL's notification register - products leaving the Czech market for good, with 'inefficient production - low volumes' among cited reasons. Each exit narrows therapeutic alternatives that pharmacies and prescribers depend on during the parallel wave of interruptions.
notes: MR dataset 15.08.2026: TYP=ukonceni podle roku DATUM_HLASENI: 2025=767, 2026 (do 15.8.)=474; duvod mj. 'Neefektivita vyroby - nizke odbery'.
